title: Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time
authors: Kevin Lin*, Charlie Snell*, Yu Wang, Charles Packer, Sarah Wooders, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez (* equal). Affiliations: 1 Letta, 2 UC Berkeley. Contact research@letta.com (title block, p.1)
venue: arXiv preprint (no venue stated on the vendored text)

problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: Test-time scaling buys accuracy but pays in latency and dollars, and the paper attributes this to a modelling assumption rather than to an unavoidable cost: 'These drawbacks are in part due to the fact that the current approach to applying test-time compute assumes that problems are stateless, i.e. queries (user queries at test-time) and the contexts (background information) required for answering them are provided to the model together at test-time.' [letta-stc §1, p.1]. Under that assumption, 'if multiple related queries require making similar inferences about the context at test-time, the model will have to recompute redundant computations each time, incurring additional latency and cost.' [letta-stc §1, p.1]
problem_stated.the_counter_observation: 'In reality, many LLM applications are inherently stateful, and work in conjunction with persisted, re-used context.' Named instances: document QA, coding agents on a common repository, conversational assistants holding dialogue history. 'In all these applications, there is context (available documents, a codebase, or conversation history) that is already available before the next user input.' [letta-stc §1, p.1]
problem_stated.the_operational_question: Given that the prompt decomposes as p = (c, q) with c available before q, what does compute spent on c alone buy at test-time? [letta-stc §3, p.3]
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] The paper defines its own gap rather than inheriting one. The stateless assumption it attacks is not quoted from any cited paper; it is the paper's own characterisation of Snell et al. 2024 / OpenAI 2024 / DeepSeek-AI 2024. See inherited_open_question.

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: Letta STC instantiates (U-E) alone, with the write operator specialised to destructive overwrite of a single text block and the retrieval operator specialised to the identity, while Theta and W are held frozen throughout.

notation_conflicts.preamble: The paper contains ZERO numbered equations. Its mechanism is stated as three inline arrow expressions in prose in §3 (p.3-4). Therefore every 'original equation number' citation below is a section/appendix locator, not an Eq. number. This absence is itself recorded under unfavorable_facts.

equations_unified.gloss: The paper's founding move: the prompt is declared decomposable into a pre-existing context and a query. Everything else follows from this declaration.
equations_unified.source: [letta-stc §3, p.3, prose — no equation number exists]

equations_unified.gloss: Standard test-time compute. The whole raw context is placed in the prompt; retrieval is the identity map. Budget $B_t$ is large.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{sleep write (U-E):}\qquad E^{(j)} \;=\; \mathrm{wr}\big(E^{(j-1)},\ \hat c^{(j)}\big) \;=\; \hat c^{(j)}, \qquad \hat c^{(j)} \;=\; S\big(E^{(j-1)};\ B_s/J\big), \qquad j = 1,\ldots,J,\ \ J \le 10
equations_unified.paper_form: $S(c) \to c'$, implemented as up to ten calls of `rethink_memory`
equations_unified.gloss: The canonical (U-E) write is instantiated three times over: (i) $\mathrm{wr}$ is DESTRUCTIVE OVERWRITE, not append or merge — the new string replaces the block wholesale; (ii) $S$ is not a single shot but an iterated self-rewrite of depth $J \le 10$; (iii) $S$ is a prompt, not a trained module — the operator is the frozen backbone conditioned on the fixed system prompt of Figure 17 (Figure 18 for AIME).
equations_unified.source: [letta-stc §3 'Sleep-time compute', p.4] + [letta-stc App. K, p.27: 'The rethink memory function takes as input a new string, and replaces the current context c and replaces the current context with the new string... The model is allowed to call the function rethink memory for up to 10 times.'] + [letta-stc App. F, Listing 1, p.22: `agent_state.memory.update_block_value(label=target_block_label, value=new_memory)`]

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{wake read (R):}\qquad \hat y \;=\; f_{B_t^{\mathrm{lo}}}\big(q;\ \Theta,\ W,\ \mathrm{ret}(E_1,q)\big), \qquad \mathrm{ret}(E_1,q) = E_1 = \hat c^{(J)}, \qquad B_t^{\mathrm{lo}} \ll B_t
equations_unified.gloss: The claim of the paper in one line: the same read map with a much smaller wake budget, because the store now holds pre-computed intermediate results. Note $\mathrm{ret}$ is again the identity — there is no index, no embedding, no scoring, no top-$m$. $\hat c$ is substituted for $c$ in the prompt verbatim.
equations_unified.source: [letta-stc §3, p.4: 'we can provide the new context c′ at test-time in place of c']

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{parallel sleep scaling:}\qquad \hat c_i \;=\; S\big(E_0;\ B_s/\kappa_{\parallel}\big),\ \ i=1,\ldots,\kappa_{\parallel}, \qquad E_1 \;=\; \mathrm{concat}\big(\hat c_1,\ldots,\hat c_{\kappa_{\parallel}}\big), \qquad \kappa_{\parallel}\in\{1,2,5,10\}
equations_unified.paper_form: 'we run k parallel generations, given input c, resulting in $c_1,\ldots,c_k$. At test-time, the model then receives the inputs concatenated $c_1,\ldots,c_k$'
equations_unified.gloss: The knob used to scale $B_s$ for non-reasoning models. Under the unified frame this is $\mathrm{wr}$ = CONCATENATION rather than overwrite, so the paper actually uses two different write operators without naming the difference: overwrite within a sleep trajectory (L3), concatenation across parallel trajectories (L5). State size grows linearly in $\kappa_{\parallel}$.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{reasoning-model sleep scaling:}\qquad B_s \ \text{varied by API `reasoning effort'} \in \{\text{low},\ \text{medium},\ \text{high}\}\ \ (\text{o1, o3-mini})
equations_unified.gloss: For reasoning models $B_s$ is an opaque vendor-side ordinal, not a token count.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{frozen layers:}\qquad \Theta_{k+1} = \Theta_k \ \ \forall k, \qquad W_t = W_{t-1} \ \ \forall t \quad (\text{$W$ does not exist in this architecture})
equations_unified.gloss: Not stated as an equation in the paper, but forced by the setup: every subject model is a closed vendor API (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o1, o3-mini, Claude Sonnet 3.7, DeepSeek-R1) and no training, fine-tuning, adapter, or optimizer appears anywhere in the paper. The paper's own words for the alternative it did not take: 'Unlike traditional representation learning, which typically operates in model parameter or activation space, we instead form representations in the space of natural language.'
equations_unified.source: [letta-stc §4.2, p.5] + [letta-stc §7 'Sleep-time compute as representation learning over tokens', p.13]

equations_unified.paper_form: 'we consider a simple linear model where tokens generated at test-time are a factor t the cost of the tokens at sleep-time. In our analysis, we set t = 10'
equations_unified.gloss: This is S0 identity (A), $C_{\mathrm{avg}} = C_{\mathrm{wake}} + C_{\mathrm{sleep}}/N_q$, with an explicit wake/sleep price ratio inserted. CRITICAL READING: both terms count GENERATED tokens only. Input/prefill tokens appear in no term, although $\hat c$ is longer than $c$ and, at $\kappa_{\parallel}=10$, ten concatenated re-representations are prefilled on every query. See systems_implications and unfavorable_facts.
equations_unified.source: [letta-stc §5.3, p.8, and footnote 4 pointing at a Databricks provisioned-throughput docs page as the justification for $\kappa_{\mathrm{cost}}=10$]

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{allocation signal (analysis only):}\qquad \pi(q\mid E_0) \;=\; \log P_{\mathrm{Llama2\text{-}70B\ base}}\big(q \mid c\big)
equations_unified.gloss: The paper's proposed predictor of when (U-E) pays: the log-probability of the query given the context under a frozen third-party base model. Used only to bin results into five quantiles; never used to gate or allocate compute.

what_is_NOT_in_the_mechanism: No retrieval index, no embedding, no similarity search, no top-k selection. $\mathrm{ret}$ is the identity. [inferred from §3, p.4: c' is provided 'in place of c']
No eviction, expiry, compaction, or capacity bound on $E$ beyond the $J \le 10$ rewrite cap. [App. K, p.27]
No cross-context or cross-session state. $E$ is scoped to one context and dies with it. [§3, p.3-4; no persistence discussion anywhere]

No verification of $\hat c$. Nothing checks whether the inferences written into the block are correct. The level-4 verbosity prompt asks the MODEL to 'first recompute and double check your answers' if it uses numbers from the block [Figure 16, p.17], which is the paper's only nod at write-correctness — and it moves the checking cost back to wake-time.
No gradient, no optimizer, no weight delta, no adapter, no fine-tuning anywhere in the paper.

Every 'learnable object' is either (a) a frozen vendor model, (b) a hand-written prompt, or (c) a hand-swept hyperparameter. The only thing that moves at all is a block of text, and it moves at sleep-time.

outer_vs_inner.reader_takeaway: [note-writer] For the monograph reader who has never trained a model, this is the cleanest possible entry point into the three-layer frame: the E-path can be demonstrated end-to-end without a single backward pass. Everything that would require T1-T5 of Part I is absent here — and that absence is exactly what makes this chapter the right first stop before the W- and Theta-path chapters, where the same idea costs a gradient.

how_this_paper_differs_from_the_canonica: $\mathrm{wr}$ = DESTRUCTIVE OVERWRITE. The canonical $\mathrm{wr}$ is unspecified and would normally admit append/merge/index-insert. Here the reference implementation literally sets the block value: `agent_state.memory.update_block_value(label=target_block_label, value=new_memory)` [App. F Listing 1, p.22], and App. K says the function 'replaces the current context c ... with the new string' [p.27]. Consequence: the store has no history and no rollback; a bad rewrite is unrecoverable within the sleep phase.

$S$ is ITERATED, not single-shot. Depth $J \le 10$, each step reading the current block plus one designated source block, terminated by the model calling `finish_rethinking` [App. K, p.27; Figure 17, p.18]. The canonical form writes $B_s$ as one budget; here it is spent over a sequential chain, which matters for sleep-phase wall-clock (see systems_implications).

A SECOND, DIFFERENT $\mathrm{wr}$ appears in the scaling experiment: across $\kappa_{\parallel}$ parallel trajectories the write is CONCATENATION, not overwrite [§5.2, p.8]. The paper does not remark on using two write operators. State size then grows linearly in $\kappa_{\parallel}$, and the non-monotonicity at $\kappa_{\parallel}=10$ (§5.2: '5 parallel generations generally outperforms 10') is the first visible cost of that growth.

$\mathrm{ret}$ is the IDENTITY. The canonical read (R) writes $\mathrm{ret}(E,q)$, implying selection. Here the entire store is spliced into the prompt in place of $c$ [§3, p.4]. There is no retriever to tune and no retrieval failure mode — which also means none of the E-path's usual retrieval costs are exercised or measured.

$E$ is CONTEXT-SCOPED and EPHEMERAL. One store per context, never persisted, never merged across contexts, never re-consolidated. The paper flags this itself as the boundary of the work: 'we make the simplifying assumption that interactions fall into two phases: sleep-time and test-time. However, real-world LLM use cases can be more complex, with multiple rounds of interaction and context modifications between rounds' [§7, p.13].

$k$ (the round index of the canonical form) never exceeds 1. There is exactly ONE sleep round in every experiment. Repeated (U-E) application is not tested anywhere in the paper — which is why $\rho$ is not merely unmeasured but out of scope by construction.

other_layers.U-W: not touched — $W$ does not exist in the architectures used
other_layers.U-Theta: not touched — every subject model is a frozen closed API. The paper gestures at (U-Theta) exactly once, as future work: 'future work could explore using sleep-time compute to help amortize some of this cost across related queries, or using the output of sleep-time compute itself as a form of synthetic data' [§7, p.13], i.e. feeding $\hat c$ into $\mathcal{R}_k$ of (U-Theta).

update_layer.ordering: Single-layer, single-round: $E_0 \to E_1$ at sleep, then read. No interleaving, no cascade, no cross-layer transfer.

B_s.detail: The paper reports NO sleep-time token count, FLOP count, or dollar figure anywhere — not in text, not on any axis, not in any table. Every figure's x-axis is 'Avg. Test Time Tokens / Question'; sleep-time cost never gets an axis of its own. What IS reported is ordinal knobs only: $J \le 10$ `rethink_memory` calls [App. K, p.27]; $\kappa_{\parallel} \in \{1,2,5,10\}$ parallel generations [§5.2, p.8; Fig. 7 legend, p.10]; sleep-time reasoning effort $\in$ {low, medium, high} [§5.2, p.8; Fig. 8 legend, p.10]. The x-axis of Figure 9 ('Total Inference Cost / Query', values around $10^2$) is a DERIVED composite $\kappa_{\mathrm{cost}}\cdot B_t + B_s/N_q$, so $B_s$ is entangled inside it and cannot be read out.
B_s.finding: The numerator of the entire amortisation argument is never given a number. S0 §2.4 calls $B_s$ '상각 가능성의 분자' — this paper, which named the line, does not report it.

L_w.detail: No wall-clock latency, TTFT, or ms/token is measured anywhere in the paper. Grep over the full text returns latency only in motivational prose and in two external URLs. Motivational claims, both uncited-by-measurement: 'waiting potentially several minutes for answers and costing up to tens of dollars per query' [§1, p.1, footnote 1 → an OpenAI o1-pro pricing page]; 'latency optimized inference can be roughly 10× more expensive' [§5.3, p.8, footnote 4 → a Databricks provisioned-throughput docs page]. The paper's ONLY latency proxy is generated test-time tokens per question.
L_w.proxy_values_actually_reported: Test-time token axes: Stateful GSM-Symbolic ≈ 0–600 tokens/question [Fig. 3, p.6]; Stateful AIME ≈ 1000–22500 depending on model [Fig. 4, p.7]; SWE-Features 3000–10000 [Fig. 11, p.12]. Headline reduction in that proxy: ~5× [Abstract; §5.1, p.6]; ~1.5× on SWE-Features [§6, p.12].

C.detail: No byte count, no character count, no token count for $\hat c$, no per-session or per-user state size anywhere. The store is a text block whose size is never reported. The only structural bounds stated are $J \le 10$ rewrites [App. K, p.27] and the Letta core-memory block layout (persona / human read-only blocks, rethink_memory read-write block) described in prose in the sleep prompt [Fig. 17, p.18]. The dataset-size numbers in Table 1 (p.19) are corpus statistics, not state capacity.
C.finding: S0 §2.4 wants $C$ in bytes/session as 'memory-device 기회의 근거'. For the E-path's founding paper this quantity is simply not on the page — which the monograph should report as the reason the E-path cannot be sized against the Theta-path from primary sources.

rho.detail: Exactly one sleep round is performed in every experiment. No repeated consolidation, no re-sleep on an updated context, no degradation measurement. Not merely unmeasured — excluded by construction, and the paper says so: 'real-world LLM use cases can be more complex, with multiple rounds of interaction and context modifications between rounds... Future work should extend sleep-time compute paradigm to more elegantly handle these scenarios' [§7, p.13]. The nearest thing to a degradation signal is the non-monotone $\kappa_{\parallel}$ result ('5 parallel generations generally outperforms 10' [§5.2, p.8]), but that is within-round breadth, not across-round decay.

N_q.value: reported only as an experimental sweep, never as a measured deployment quantity
N_q.detail: $N_q \in \{1, 2, 5, 10\}$ questions per context, constructed synthetically [§5.3, p.8-9; Fig. 9, p.11]. No distribution of $N_q$ from any real workload is reported. This is the S0 §7 caveat confirmed at source: the amortisation identity (A) is exercised only at values the authors chose.

experiments.no_result_tables_exist: The paper contains exactly ONE table (Table 1, p.19, dataset statistics). Every accuracy, F1, and cost number is presented as an unannotated line plot. No numeric result table, no error bars, no confidence intervals, no dispersion statistics appear anywhere. Consequently the precise operating-point values below are limited to what the paper states in prose plus the axis ranges printed on the figures.

headline_numbers.claim: Sleep-time compute beats pass@k parallel test-time scaling at equal test-time token budget
headline_numbers.exact_wording: 'across all tasks and models, sleep-time compute consistently outperforms pass@k parallel scaling at the same test-time token budget'
headline_numbers.strength_of_the_baseline_as_stated_by_au: pass@k 'makes the unrealistic assumption of having oracle query access to a ground truth verifier at test-time, an assumption which we do not make with sleep-time compute. Therefore, outperforming the pass@k baseline would represent a meaningful improvement' — i.e. the authors correctly note they beat an ORACLE-ADVANTAGED baseline. Applied only 'to the lowest sequential compute setting on each task'.

headline_numbers.claim: SWE-Features: up to ~1.5× decrease in test-time tokens at low budgets
headline_numbers.exact_wording: 'at lower test-time compute budgets, leveraging sleep-time compute can improve performance, achieving up to roughly a 1.5× decrease in test-time tokens. However, when the test-time compute budget is high, using only test-time compute can perform better.'
headline_numbers.figure_ranges: F1 axis ≈ 0.30–0.55; test-time token axis 3000–10000 [Fig. 11, p.12]

headline_numbers.claim: Query predictability correlates with sleep-time-compute benefit
headline_numbers.exact_wording: 'the accuracy gap between sleep-time compute and standard test-time compute widens as the questions become more predictable from the context'
headline_numbers.protocol: 5 quantile bins of $\log P(q\mid c)$ under Llama2-70B base; GPT-4o-mini; 'Verbosity 0' prompt (lowest test-time budget). Accuracy-delta axes: P1 spans 0.0–0.5, P2 spans 0.00–0.40 [Fig. 10, p.11].

headline_numbers.claim: The questions are not trivially guessable from context
headline_numbers.exact_wording: 'sleep-time compute significantly outperforms the context-only baseline, demonstrating that the questions in our datasets are not trivially predictable from the context'
headline_numbers.note: Figure 22's legend labels this baseline 'ablate question'

negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.result: At HIGH test-time budgets on Stateful GSM-Symbolic the baseline WINS
negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.exact_wording: 'However, at the test-tome [sic] compute budgets, the test-time compute only baseline slightly outperforms sleep-time compute. We hypothesize that this may be because the standard test-time compute only has the content relevant to the specific question, so there is less distracting information in the prompt.'
'On all models, we see a significant test-time, accuracy pareto shift from applying sleep-time compute, with the exception of o1, which demonstrates limited gains.'
'there seems to be a limit to the number of parallel agents that can improve performance, as we find that 5 parallel generations generally outperforms 10'
negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.status: no threshold characterised, no explanation offered

negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.result: On the realistic agentic task the baseline has better precision at high budget
negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.exact_wording: 'in the high test-time budget setting standard test-time compute has higher precision and comparable recall. We hypothesize that, using only test-time compute tends to begin editing files earlier and usually edits fewer files overall. In contrast, the agent with sleep-time compute, having explored more files during the test-time phase, tends to edit more files, which may lead to slightly lower precision.'
negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.note: the sentence says 'explored more files during the test-time phase', which appears to be a slip for the sleep-time phase

negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.result: Fewer queries per context makes sleep-time compute a net loss
negative_and_qualifying_results_reported.exact_wording: 'When there are fewer questions per context, we see that it is less favorable to use sleep-time compute, in terms of total cost.'

scale_ceiling.model_size: Unknown by construction. Every subject model is a closed vendor API with undisclosed parameter count (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, o1, o3-mini, Claude Sonnet 3.7, DeepSeek-R1) [§4.2, p.5]. The only parameter count stated anywhere in the paper is Llama2-70B, used purely as a log-probability scorer for the predictability analysis, never as a subject [§5.4, p.9]. The paper therefore establishes no model-scale ceiling at all — the method is model-agnostic prompting, and its scale claim is neither confirmed nor refuted by anything on the page.
scale_ceiling.training_data_scale: Zero. No training of any kind occurs.
scale_ceiling.evaluation_scale: Largest: Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic P1 — 12043 questions over 1095 contexts, of which 10948 (90.9%) are o3-mini-generated [Table 1, p.19]. Stateful GSM-Symbolic P1 = 5000 examples, P2 = 2500 [§4.1, p.4]. Stateful AIME = 60 questions [§4.1, p.4].
scale_ceiling.realism_ceiling: SWE-Features: 33 pull requests from 2 repositories, scored by file-set F1 rather than by tests [§6, p.12; App. D, pp.19-20]. This is the paper's only non-math, non-synthetic evaluation, and it is also the setting where the gain is smallest (~1.5× vs ~5×) and reverses at high budget.
scale_ceiling.context_length_ceiling: Not reported. No context length, prompt length, or $|\hat c|$ figure appears anywhere. GSM-Symbolic contexts are a few sentences (see Fig. 2, p.5 and Fig. 20, p.20); SWE-Features contexts are PR titles/bodies/patches plus agent repository exploration [App. D, p.20]. No long-context regime is exercised, which is notable for a paper whose motivating examples are codebases and document QA.
scale_ceiling.deployment_gap: [note-writer] The paper's own motivating scenarios — a coding assistant over a large repo, a conversational assistant over dialogue history — are evaluated at 33 PRs and zero dialogue sessions respectively.

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: compute applied to a context $c$ during the idle interval before the query $q$ arrives, producing a re-represented context $\hat c$ used at wake-time
new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.note: This is the name that created the line. The monograph's operational definition (S0 §2.3) generalises it away from $E$; the chapter must show that generalisation explicitly.

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: the decomposition of a prompt into pre-existing context and query, and the claim that the test-time-scaling literature implicitly assumes it is impossible
the sharing of one $\hat c$ across $N_q$ queries about the same context, giving $\mathrm{Cost}_{\mathrm{avg}} = \kappa_{\mathrm{cost}} B_t + B_s/N_q$
$\log P(q\mid c)$ under a frozen base LM, proposed as the signal for when sleep-time compute pays
the Letta operator and the mutable text block it overwrites
new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.source: [App. F, p.22; App. K, p.27; Fig. 17, p.18]

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.term: Stateful GSM-Symbolic / Stateful AIME / Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic / SWE-Features

renamed_or_corrected_for_the_monograph.problem: nothing is learned; no gradient exists in this paper
renamed_or_corrected_for_the_monograph.note: S0 §7 already lists this as an obligatory caveat for chapter E-2. The paper's own body is correct and explicit — the misleading word appears only in the figure label and, arguably, in the §7 'representation learning' framing.

renamed_or_corrected_for_the_monograph.problem: all collide with reserved symbols (see core_mechanism.notation_conflicts)

extended.extension: the paper's own name for the E-path, defined by contrast with the other two: 'Unlike traditional representation learning (Bengio et al., 2014), which typically operates in model parameter or activation space, we instead form representations in the space of natural language.' [§7, p.13]
extended.monograph_use: This single sentence is the best primary-source warrant for S0's three-path split, stated by an E-path author. Parameter space = $\Theta$; activation space = $W$; natural-language space = $E$.

inherited_open_question.justification: The paper quotes no prior work's open question, and its Related Work (§2, pp.3) is organised by technique family (test-time scaling; speculative decoding; pre-computation) rather than by an unresolved question handed forward. The closest thing to a lineage statement is a lineage of ANALOGY, not of open problems: 'sleep-time compute builds on the idea of pre-fetching in traditional operating systems, in the context of LLMs à la Packer et al. (2023), storing frequently used computational results to avoid higher latency at test-time.' [§2 'Pre-computation', p.3]. Packer et al. 2023 is MemGPT — the same authors and the same company (Letta) — and no open question from MemGPT is quoted or paraphrased.
inherited_open_question.what_it_implicitly_answers_instead: It manufactures its gap by naming an assumption inside the test-time-scaling literature (Snell et al. 2024; OpenAI 2024; DeepSeek-AI 2024; Brown et al. 2024) that none of those papers states as an open question: 'These drawbacks are in part due to the fact that the current approach to applying test-time compute assumes that problems are stateless, i.e. queries ... and the contexts ... are provided to the model together at test-time. In practice, this means that if multiple related queries require making similar inferences about the context at test-time, the model will have to recompute redundant computations each time.' [§1, p.1]. The implicit question answered is therefore: *is the test-time budget the right axis at all, given that the context arrives first?*
inherited_open_question.bridge_in_material_for_chapter_E2: [note-writer] The bridge chain of S0 §5 runs MemGPT → Letta STC. Since the paper does not quote MemGPT's open question, chapter E-2's §1 must open on the *un-inherited* question — that is a legitimate bridge and an honest one: the E-path's founding paper opens a gap rather than closing one, and the monograph should say so rather than manufacture a false inheritance. The one genuine textual link to MemGPT is the OS/pre-fetching analogy in §2, and the shared authorship (Packer, Wooders, Lin, Stoica, Gonzalez appear on both).

open_questions.question: Which contexts have predictable queries, and how should compute be split between sleep and wake across a heterogeneous workload?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'An interesting direction for future work is identifying which contexts may have predictable questions and optimally allocating inference compute between sleep-time and test-time across different contexts and queries.'
open_questions.source: [§7 'Query predictability and allocating sleep-time compute', p.13]
open_questions.bridge_out: the allocation policy is the missing controller — nothing in the paper decides WHEN to sleep

open_questions.question: How does the paradigm extend past the two-phase context/query split — multiple interaction rounds, context edits between rounds, and sleep intervals ranging from typing pauses to days?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'we make the simplifying assumption that interactions fall into two phases: sleep-time and test-time. However, real-world LLM use cases can be more complex, with multiple rounds of interaction and context modifications between rounds (e.g. multiple edits to a code-base). Moreover, the length of the sleep-time may also vary significantly between interactions (eg. short spans between user typing or days of inactivity). Future work should extend sleep-time compute paradigm to more elegantly handle these scenarios.'
open_questions.bridge_out: this is exactly the $\rho$ question of S0 §2.4 — repeated (U-E) rounds — stated by the authors as unaddressed

open_questions.question: Can sleep-time compute be understood and pushed as representation learning in natural-language space rather than parameter or activation space?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'Unlike traditional representation learning (Bengio et al., 2014), which typically operates in model parameter or activation space, we instead form representations in the space of natural language. ... Future work should further explore the potential for sleep-time compute to enable the learning of useful natural language representations.'
open_questions.source: [§7 'Sleep-time compute as representation learning over tokens', p.13]
open_questions.bridge_out: THE fork of the whole monograph, named by an E-path author: parameter space = Theta-path, activation space = W-path, natural-language space = E-path

open_questions.question: Can the output of sleep-time compute serve as synthetic pretraining data, amortising synthetic-data cost?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'future work could explore using sleep-time compute to help amortize some of this cost across related queries, or using the output of sleep-time compute itself as a form of synthetic data.'
open_questions.source: [§7 'Synthetic data generation via sleep-time compute', p.13]
open_questions.bridge_out: the explicit E→Theta hand-off: $\hat c$ becomes $\mathcal{R}_k$ in (U-Theta). The paper proposes the composition and never tests it.

open_questions.question: Why does the benefit invert at high test-time budgets?
open_questions.status: hypothesis offered ('less distracting information in the prompt'), never tested
open_questions.source: [§5.1, p.6; and the same reversal recurs on SWE-Features, §6, p.12]

open_questions.question: Why is sleep-time scaling non-monotone — why does $\kappa_{\parallel}=5$ beat $\kappa_{\parallel}=10$?
open_questions.status: observed, no mechanism proposed, no threshold characterised

open_questions.question: Why does o1 gain little when every other reasoning model gains a lot?
What is $N_q$ in a real deployment?
open_questions.status: never measured; swept over {1,2,5,10} on a synthetic dataset. The entire amortisation claim is conditional on this unknown.

open_questions.question: Is $\kappa_{\mathrm{cost}}=10$ (test-time tokens cost 10× sleep-time tokens) right, and does it hold across providers and hardware?
open_questions.status: asserted from an external vendor docs page, never measured

open_questions.question: How is $\hat c$ validated, expired, evicted, or versioned?
open_questions.status: not addressed anywhere. There is no write-verification step, no capacity policy, no staleness handling.
open_questions.source: [absent — inferred from the total absence of any such discussion in §3, §7, App. F, App. K]

open_questions.question: Does the benefit survive when the context is genuinely long (a real repository, a long document, a long dialogue) rather than a few sentences?
open_questions.status: not addressed; no context-length figure appears in the paper
open_questions.source: [absent; motivating examples in §1, p.1 are far larger than anything evaluated]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Both headline benchmarks are author-constructed variants of existing datasets, made specifically to exhibit the effect. Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME exist only because the authors cut existing problems into a context half and a query half.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the 5×, 13% and 18% numbers have no independent benchmark behind them; there is no pre-existing stateful reasoning benchmark in the paper

unfavorable_facts.fact: Stateful AIME construction involved undisclosed-count manual intervention, including instances whose context is EMPTY.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'There are a couple of edge cases where the question is posed in e.g. the second to last statement rather than the last statement. In these cases, we manually rearrange the statements to ensure the query being used corresponds to the question. In a few cases, there is only one statement in the problem. In these cases, the context is empty.' Also: LaTeX figures were manually stripped after manual solvability checks.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: empty-context instances are ones on which sleep-time compute can do nothing by construction, and the count is never given, out of only 60 questions

unfavorable_facts.fact: The 2.5× amortisation result rests on a dataset that is 90.9% model-generated, with no validation of the generated answers reported.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: Multi-Query GSM-Symbolic P1: 10948 of 12043 questions generated by o3-mini; P2: 4997 of 5497. Both = 90.9%.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: $N_q$, the denominator of the amortisation identity, is itself synthetic; and the generated questions are, by inspection of the paper's own example, systematically easier and more context-local than the original (e.g. 'How many stacking rings are on the tower?' is answerable by copying a number out of the context)
unfavorable_facts.source: [Table 1, p.19; §4.1, p.4; App. C Fig. 19, p.19; example set in Fig. 20, p.20]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The 2.5× is a model output, not a measurement. It is produced by a linear cost model with an assumed constant $\kappa_{\mathrm{cost}}=10$ justified by a link to a Databricks provisioned-throughput documentation page, not by any measurement in the paper.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'Since at test-time, there are strict latency constraints, and latency optimized inference can be roughly 10× more expensive, we model the total cost of inference between both sleep-time and test-time, by up-weighing the cost of test-time tokens.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: at $\kappa_{\mathrm{cost}}=1$ the amortisation advantage would shrink substantially, and the paper reports no sensitivity analysis over $\kappa_{\mathrm{cost}}$

unfavorable_facts.fact: The cost model counts GENERATED tokens only. Prefill/input tokens appear in no term — yet the method's whole mechanism is to make the input longer.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'a simple linear model where tokens generated at test-time are a factor t the cost of the tokens at sleep-time'; and every figure axis reads 'Avg. Test Time Tokens / Question'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: $\hat c$ is visibly longer than $c$ (compare the two context boxes in Fig. 1, p.2), and under parallel scaling the wake-time prompt contains $\kappa_{\parallel}$ concatenated re-representations — up to ten — on EVERY query [§5.2, p.8]. That input cost is invisible in the 5×, the 13%, the 18% and the 2.5×.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The advantage reverses at high test-time budget, on both the synthetic task and the realistic one.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: GSM-Symbolic: 'at the test-tome [sic] compute budgets, the test-time compute only baseline slightly outperforms sleep-time compute'. SWE-Features: 'when the test-time compute budget is high, using only test-time compute can perform better', with 'standard test-time compute has higher precision and comparable recall'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the pareto claim is regime-restricted; the paper's abstract does not carry this restriction

unfavorable_facts.fact: Scaling the proposed component is non-monotone — more sleep-time compute can make things worse.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'there seems to be a limit to the number of parallel agents that can improve performance, as we find that 5 parallel generations generally outperforms 10'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the 13% headline comes from this same sweep; the best setting is interior and no rule is given for finding it

unfavorable_facts.fact: The strongest reasoning model tested barely benefits.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'with the exception of o1, which demonstrates limited gains'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: suggests the gain may be substituting for reasoning capability rather than adding to it, and the paper offers no analysis

unfavorable_facts.fact: Models were selected on a criterion correlated with the outcome being measured.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'On each dataset, we evaluate models which have poor performance when using a small amount of test-time compute, but yield improvements from scaling up test-time compute.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the model pool is chosen for having a steep test-time-compute/accuracy slope, which is exactly the property that makes a 5× horizontal shift look large

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper contains no result table and no dispersion statistics. One table exists (Table 1) and it is dataset statistics.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: every quantitative claim in the abstract must be read off an unannotated line plot. Runs were averaged (3 for o1/o3-mini/R1; 10 for Claude 3.7 Sonnet) but no standard deviation, error bar, or confidence interval is reported anywhere — while the AIME set is only 60 questions, so one question is 1.67 accuracy points.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The Claude run count was raised from 3 to 10 post hoc, on the basis of observed noise.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'We average results over 3 runs for o1, o3-mini and R1. For Claude 3.7 Sonnet, we average over 10 runs as we observed more noise in initial experiments.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: unequal, outcome-informed sampling effort across arms, with no dispersion reported to let a reader judge it

unfavorable_facts.fact: Appendix A shows only test-time prompts that presuppose the sleep-time artefact. All five verbosity prompts (levels 0-4) instruct the model to 'check the rethink memory block' and 'Do not recompute anything that already exists in the rethink memory block.' The corresponding baseline-arm prompts are not shown.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: from the text alone one cannot verify that the two arms differ ONLY in the presence of $\hat c$; if the baseline received the same prompt, it was told to consult a block that does not exist
unfavorable_facts.source: [App. A, Figs. 12-16, pp.16-17; §5.1, p.6 says 'The full prompts are in Appendix A']

unfavorable_facts.fact: In the vendored text extraction, the level-2 (Figure 14) and level-3 (Figure 15) verbosity prompts are character-for-character identical.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: if this is real and not an extraction artefact, then two of the five x-axis operating points for the non-reasoning models were produced by the same prompt, and the GSM-Symbolic compute axis has fewer distinct settings than it appears
unfavorable_facts.hedge: this must be checked against the published PDF before being asserted in the monograph — see todo_verify
unfavorable_facts.source: [App. A, Fig. 14 (p.16) vs Fig. 15 (p.17), verified identical by string comparison over the vendored text]

unfavorable_facts.fact: SWE-Features — the only realistic evaluation — is n=33 from 2 repositories, and is scored without running any tests.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'Since the PRs are scraped from GitHub, there are not straightforward tests to use for evaluation. Instead, we compare the predicted set of modified files with the ground truth list of modified files, and report the F1 score'. The agent IS told to write tests in Docker, but 'after the agent makes the modifications, we extract the modified files and calculate the F1 score'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the metric rewards guessing the right file set, not producing working code; and it is the metric on which the method's advantage is smallest and reverses at high budget

unfavorable_facts.fact: In SWE-Features, the same model family that solves the task also DEFINES the task's context: claude-sonnet-3-7-20250219 clusters the PRs to decide which prior PRs count as 'related context' for a target PR, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet is the agent evaluated in Figure 11.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: what counts as usefully-related context is set by the same model that must exploit it; no control for this is reported

unfavorable_facts.fact: A prompt-engineering confound is disclosed inside the SWE-Features setup and never ablated.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'We found that explicitly indicating the current and total steps significantly improves agent performance, especially in low-budget settings.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the low-budget regime is precisely where sleep-time compute is claimed to win, and an admitted large prompt effect operates there

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper's motivating quantity — latency — is never measured. Zero wall-clock, TTFT, or ms/token numbers appear. The claim 'waiting potentially several minutes' is footnoted to an OpenAI pricing page and the '10× more expensive' claim to a Databricks docs page.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the abstract's framing ('comes with high latency and inference cost') is supported entirely by a generated-token proxy
unfavorable_facts.source: [§1, p.1 + fn 1; §5.3, p.8 + fn 4; whole-text grep for latency/ms/seconds returns only prose]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Nothing is learned and nothing persists. The store is destroyed with the context; no gradient, adapter, or weight delta exists; the write is a destructive overwrite with no history.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: not a flaw in the paper — the paper is explicit — but it bounds what the monograph may claim for the E-path. Figure 1's label 'Learned Context' is the one place where the paper's own presentation overstates.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The composition the paper proposes with the Theta-path — using $\hat c$ as synthetic pretraining data — is stated as future work and never tested.
unfavorable_facts.exact_wording: 'future work could explore ... using the output of sleep-time compute itself as a form of synthetic data'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: S0 §7 requires flagging untested cross-path compositions; this is one, proposed by the authors themselves

unfavorable_facts.fact: Internal referencing slips. §5.2 attributes the 18% AIME result to 'Figure 26', which is the AIME-2025-only appendix figure; §4.1 and App. C refer to 'Table C' for a table captioned 'Table 1'; §6 says the sleep-arm agent 'explored more files during the test-time phase' where the sleep-time phase is meant; §5.1 contains the typo 'at the test-tome compute budgets' in the sentence stating the adverse result.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the adverse-result sentence is also the least carefully typeset one in the paper, and the 18% pointer resolves to a subset figure

unfavorable_facts.fact: The amortisation experiment uses a ~20% subsample of the base datasets.
unfavorable_facts.numbers: Multi-Query is built from 1095 contexts (of GSM-Symbolic P1's 5000 examples) and 500 contexts (of P2's 2500), because 'We sample one instance from each template'.

cross_path_citations.verdict: Near-total silence toward the W-path and the Theta-path, and complete silence toward the biological/CLS ancestry whose vocabulary the paper borrows for its own title.
full_bibliography: Gunasekar et al. 2023 (Textbooks Are All You Need, 2306.11644)

W_path.citations: ZERO. Not one paper on fast weights, test-time training, TTT/Titans/Miras/Atlas, linear attention, state-space models, recurrent memory, or any weight-space test-time state.
W_path.note: The word 'state' appears in the paper only in the sense of 'stateful application'. The KV cache is never mentioned; a whole-text grep for 'KV' and 'cache' returns only the Smith 1982 citation and unrelated PR titles from the SWE-Features corpus.

Theta_path.citations: ZERO direct. No LoRA, no PEFT, no model editing (ROME/MEMIT), no continual learning, no catastrophic forgetting, no knowledge distillation, no self-training-for-weights.
Theta_path.nearest_neighbours: Two synthetic-data papers appear, but only in the §7 future-work paragraph and only as consumers of sleep-time output, never as competing sleep-time mechanisms: Yang et al. 2024 (Synthetic continued pretraining, 2409.07431) and Gunasekar et al. 2023 (Textbooks). Bansal et al. 2024 (compute-optimal sampling for training reasoners) likewise appears only there.
Theta_path.the_one_explicit_acknowledgement: §7 (p.13) names the other two spaces without citing any work in them: 'Unlike traditional representation learning (Bengio et al., 2014), which typically operates in model parameter or activation space, we instead form representations in the space of natural language.' The only citation offered for parameter/activation-space representation is a 2014 review predating the entire modern line.

bio_CLS_path.citations: ZERO. No McClelland/CLS, no hippocampal replay, no sleep-consolidation neuroscience, no dreaming literature, no EWC/replay.
bio_CLS_path.finding: The paper's central metaphor — 'sleep' — carries no biological citation whatsoever. §1 (p.2) introduces the term purely operationally: 'inference is done between interactions with the model while it would otherwise be idle in sleep-time.' The word is chosen for idleness, not for consolidation. This is important for the monograph: the E-path adopted the sleep vocabulary WITHOUT the CLS argument, and the Theta-path papers that later reused the word did so with the biology attached. The naming collision is not a shared theoretical commitment.

E_path_internal.citations: Exactly ONE: Packer et al. 2023 (MemGPT), by the same authors at the same company, cited in §2 for the OS/pre-fetching analogy. No RAG, no vector database, no graph memory, no retrieval literature of any kind appears in the bibliography.
E_path_internal.finding: Even within its own path the paper is nearly self-referential. There is no engagement with retrieval-augmented generation at all, despite $\mathrm{ret}$ being the identity being a design choice that RAG work would contest.

cross_path_citations.what_it_DOES_engage: Test-time scaling (Snell 2024, OpenAI 2024, DeepSeek-AI 2024, Brown 2024, Muennighoff 2025), speculative decoding (Leviathan 2023, Stern 2018, Cai 2024, DeepSeek-V3), and classical systems pre-computation (Smith 1982 cache memories, Gray 1997 data cubes). The intellectual parentage the paper claims for itself is INFERENCE SYSTEMS, not memory research.
cross_path_citations.monograph_implication: [note-writer] For the S0 §5 bridge chain this is a load-bearing finding, and it should be stated as an evaluative block, not smoothed over: the paper that gave the line its name situates itself in caching and speculative decoding, not in memory or learning. Every subsequent W-path and Theta-path paper that uses the phrase 'sleep-time compute' inherits a name from a paper that never cited them and never cited the biology.

systems_implications.preamble: Grounding key: [PAPER] = a number or statement on the page with a locator; [INFERENCE] = the note-writer's translation, not in the paper. The monograph must preserve this split, because this paper supplies far fewer systems numbers than a reader of its abstract would expect.

items.claim: The mechanism is prompt-token substitution and nothing else. At wake-time the served request is byte-identical in kind to a normal request; only the prompt content differs.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §3, p.4: 'we can provide the new context c′ at test-time in place of c'. No serving-stack change is described anywhere.

items.claim: Therefore the state lands in the KV cache and in the application's text store — never in weights. Shared-weight batching is PRESERVED.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE], grounded in the mechanism above. Contrast STYLE-NOTATION §3 Rosetta row: 'per-request fast-weight state는 shared-weight batching을 깨뜨린다 → grouped-GEMM decode'. The E-path pays no such price. The paper never discusses batching, KV cache, or prefix caching — grep returns zero hits.

items.claim: $\hat c$ is a shared PREFIX across the $N_q$ queries of one context, so on any stack with prefix caching the amortisation is not merely economic but literal KV reuse.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE]. The paper's amortisation model (§5.3, p.8) counts only generated tokens and therefore captures none of this; it also captures none of the prefill cost of the longer prefix. The monograph should note that the paper's own cost model both understates the cost (no prefill) and understates the saving (no prefix cache) of its own method.

items.claim: Decode cost at wake-time falls by ~5× in generated tokens at low budgets, and by ~1.5× on the agentic task.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §5.1, p.6 and Abstract for ~5×; §6, p.12 for ~1.5×. Absolute axis ranges: GSM-Symbolic ~0-600 generated tokens/question [Fig. 3, p.6]; AIME ~1000-22500 [Fig. 4, p.7]; SWE-Features 3000-10000 [Fig. 11, p.12].

items.claim: Wake-time PREFILL rises, and the paper never bounds by how much. Under parallel sleep scaling the prompt carries $\kappa_{\parallel}$ concatenated re-representations, up to 10, on every single query.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §5.2, p.8 for the concatenation and $\kappa_{\parallel}\in\{1,2,5,10\}$. [INFERENCE] for the prefill consequence — $|\hat c|$ is never reported, so the prefill delta cannot be computed from the paper. This is the single largest systems gap in the work: a decode-token saving is claimed while an unbounded prefill-token cost is unmeasured.

items.claim: State bytes per session cannot be computed from this paper. No token count, character count, or byte figure for $\hat c$ appears.
items.grounding: [PAPER — by absence]. See cost_table.C. [INFERENCE] The order of magnitude is inferable only from Fig. 1 (p.2), where $\hat c$ for a five-clause juggler problem is roughly 70 words against a ~35-word raw context, i.e. an expansion factor around 2 on a toy input — but this is a figure illustration, not a measurement, and must not be quoted as one.

items.claim: Sleep-time work is a batchable, latency-insensitive, throughput-optimised decode job. Converting latency-critical decode into background decode IS the product, and the paper prices that conversion at 10:1.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §5.3, p.8: 'at test-time, there are strict latency constraints, and latency optimized inference can be roughly 10× more expensive' (footnote 4 → Databricks provisioned-throughput docs). [INFERENCE] For a serving fleet this is the recognisable shape of moving work from an interactive tier to a batch tier; the 10:1 is exactly the interactive-vs-provisioned-throughput price ratio, asserted rather than measured.

items.claim: Sleep-time wall-clock is NOT free even when off the critical path, because the sleep write is a SEQUENTIAL chain of up to 10 model turns per context.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. K, p.27: 'The model is allowed to call the function rethink memory for up to 10 times', each call consuming the previous block. [INFERENCE] Ten sequential turns per context bounds how many contexts a fleet can pre-warm per unit time; combined with $\kappa_{\parallel}$ up to 10 parallel trajectories, the worst configuration is 100 model turns per context before the first query arrives. The paper reports neither the turn count actually used nor any throughput figure.

items.claim: Where the traffic lands in the hierarchy: application-level text store (Letta memory blocks) → tokenizer → prefill → KV cache. Never HBM-resident weights, never optimizer state, never a per-user weight shard.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. F Listing 1, p.22 shows the store is `agent_state.memory` block values, i.e. application objects. [INFERENCE] for the hierarchy walk. This is the sharpest contrast to draw against the Theta-path in Part III: the E-path's write traffic is text into a database, the Theta-path's is a weight delta into device memory, and only the latter creates a memory-device opportunity.

items.claim: The workload signal the paper offers for admission control is $\log P(q\mid c)$ under a small frozen base model — cheap enough to run as a gate.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §5.4, p.9 (Llama2-70B base, 5 quantile bins, gap widens monotonically-in-direction across bins per Fig. 10, p.11). [INFERENCE] The paper uses it only for post-hoc binning; as a serving control it would be a single forward pass over $(c,q)$ — but note it requires $q$, which is not available at sleep-time, so it cannot gate the sleep decision as stated. The paper names the resulting problem as future work (§7, p.13) without observing this circularity.

items.claim: Economic break-even is at $N_q$ somewhere between 1 and 10 under the paper's own model; below it, sleep-time compute is a net loss.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Fig. 9 caption, p.11: 'When there are fewer questions per context, we see that it is less favorable to use sleep-time compute, in terms of total cost.' Points measured: $N_q \in \{1,2,5,10\}$; 2.5× saving reported at $N_q=10$ [§5.3, p.9]. The exact break-even $N_q$ is not stated and cannot be read reliably off the log-scale plot.

items.claim: The monograph reader's standing question — 'so what changes at decode?' — has a clean answer here, and it is the E-path's defining property: nothing about the decode kernel changes. Only the prompt changes. That is simultaneously why the E-path ships today and why it cannot raise capacity the way the Theta-path can.
items.grounding: [INFERENCE], grounded in L2-L4 and L7 of core_mechanism.
